verdict.rationale: mise defines its automations, both tasks and bootstrap machine setup, as declarative files (mise.toml and mise-tasks scripts) that are meant to be checked in, and it has its own review tooling: `mise bootstrap plan`/`status`, `--dry-run` previews, and `mise lock --bump --dry-run`. Lockfiles with `mise install --locked` pin reproducible tool versions. Versioning and rollback of the automations themselves, however, depend on external git rather than a mise feature. Missing for 10: native versioning/history of tasks and automations, a built-in rollback command, review/diff of task changes beyond bootstrap dry-runs, and independent corroboration.
